key_insight: PINNs miss shocks because the steady Euler residual encourages overly smooth solutions, so the paper reformulates shock capturing as a time-evolving process that naturally develops discontinuities.
engineering_relevance: This offers a physics-informed route to more reliable airfoil flow prediction in inviscid regimes where shock location strongly affects aerodynamic design and analysis.
method: Add unsteady Euler time-derivative terms to strengthen the physics constraint.
Use pseudo time-stepping in the PDE loss so shocks emerge gradually toward steady state.
Adopt a simplified Euler formulation to improve shock-capturing accuracy.
evidence_signal: The approach is validated on four forward problems with different flow conditions and geometries, showing improved shock-capturing performance in the reported tests.
watch_item: Training may remain sensitive to long-time unsteady evolution and the pseudo time-stepping design, which could affect stability and scalability in harder flow cases.
paper_title: Physics-informed neural networks for shock capturing in inviscid flows around an airfoil
